for: humanities/social-science MA/early-career researcher, international conference travel

funders.note: No dedicated Nigerian national research council travel grant (equivalent to India's ICSSR) was found for social-science/humanities international conference travel. TETFund (below) is the closest national scheme, but it funds academic staff, not students.

funders.name: TETFund Conference Attendance (CA) Intervention Programme
funders.eligible_who: Academic staff of TETFund beneficiary institutions (federal/state universities, polytechnics, colleges of education) with a paper accepted for presentation; NOT open to MA students in their own right
funders.amount_note: International conference travel is disbursed through the beneficiary institution, capped institutionally; not a direct-to-individual student grant
funders.cycle: Institutional call rounds, timing set by TETFund/the institution, not a fixed annual date
funders.requires: Paper accepted for presentation; conference organised by a recognised academic body; sponsorship applied for through the home institution, not directly by the researcher
funders.source_note: Real, active national scheme, but structured for academic staff sponsored through their institution -- not a fit for an MA student applying individually

funders.note: Home institution: check the University of Lagos Department of Geography or the Postgraduate School's own conference-travel support; not tracked here since it is institution-specific.

funders.name: Global South Colloquium Fund (GSCF) travel grant
funders.eligible_who: Early-career researchers, preference to those from the Global South, working in Global South studies, development studies, area studies or sociocultural studies -- broad enough to cover Niger Delta migration research
funders.amount_note: Travel grants up to a maximum of USD $500 / GBP £400, covering travel costs only (not registration, accommodation or subsistence)
funders.cycle: The 2025/2026 funding rounds are complete; the fund reopens 1 January 2027. Apply 10-12 weeks before the event once open.
funders.requires: Event registration confirmation; one delegate per institution per event
funders.source_note: Real, general-purpose Global South travel fund from the Council for European Studies / World Society Foundation; currently between funding rounds

funders.name: ASA Mahmoud Mohamed Taha Student Travel Award
funders.eligible_who: Students of African studies, to support research, exchange of ideas, or travel to present at the ASA Annual Meeting
funders.amount_note: A travel grant plus a plaque presented at the ASA Annual Meeting; exact amount not confirmed on the current page
funders.cycle: Annual, tied to the ASA Annual Meeting cycle; exact 2026 deadline not confirmed on the page fetched
funders.requires: African studies research; application through the ASA awards portal
funders.source_note: Directly relevant to the ASA 2026 candidate opportunity; a real, recurring ASA student award

funders.name: ASA Travel Support Grant
funders.eligible_who: Emerging and contingent scholars attending the ASA Annual Meeting, preference to those on the meeting programme or ICAADS sessions
funders.amount_note: Applied to travel costs or the conference hotel; exact amount not stated
funders.cycle: The page fetched is dated to the ASA 66th Annual Meeting (San Francisco) with a June 2023 deadline; the 2026 cycle's dates are not yet confirmed
funders.source_note: Page found describes a past (2023/San Francisco) cycle; the scheme likely recurs annually but current-cycle details need re-checking closer to ASA 2026

funders.note: No current destination-specific scheme found for a Nigerian early-career humanities/social-science researcher traveling to the US, Belgium or elsewhere for these particular conferences.
